source_neutral.procedure: The onboarding flow is examined by changing which components are available to users and recording how users' progress toward activation develops over elapsed time. Component availability is the factor that is deliberately set; progress toward activation over time is the measured result. The actual proposed components and their dependencies must first be identified, because none are specified in the packet. Activation is defined in observable terms, executable activation is distinguished from completion of a prototype task, and the user group, entry checkpoint, prior experience and starting progress are specified. The procedure assumes that component availability can be changed reproducibly while the other intended conditions are preserved. If a component cannot be separated from its dependencies, the coupled components are treated as a bundle and conclusions are bounded to that bundle. Overall, each tested component is made unavailable for one randomly assigned group of users, the resulting time course of progress and activation is compared with that of a group receiving the unchanged full redesign, and selected tests are repeated with a second component present and absent to examine suspected dependencies or substitution.
source_neutral.action: At a standardized checkpoint before users encounter the component being tested, record each user's initial progress. Switch that component from available to unavailable in a single change at that point, and keep it unavailable for the whole observation period. Randomly assign comparable users either to this variant or to a control receiving the unchanged full redesign, keeping other components, instructions and assistance rules fixed. Record both groups' progress over time from the checkpoint through a prespecified observation window long enough to include plausible delayed completion. Use fresh users for each subsequent variant to reduce learning carryover. Repeat selected tests with a second component present and absent, covering the full configuration, each single-removal configuration and the joint-removal configuration, to test suspected dependencies or substitution. Before data collection, define activation criteria, meaningful effect sizes, sample size, observation duration and a participant burden limit. End each individual's observation at the time limit or burden limit. Record early exits and assistance explicitly, and do not treat later outcomes that were not observed as established failures.
source_neutral.observables: Timestamped progress events, errors, retries, assistance and activation. Cumulative activation over time in each condition, and progress or activation rates per time interval, compared between conditions. Delay before progress begins; time to reach a specified activation proportion, when that proportion is reached; early maxima in rates; repeated back-and-forth movement between steps; and later differences in completion. Temporary maxima or repeated rises and falls are interpreted solely in measures that are capable of rising and falling; cumulative activation cannot exceed its later value and then fall, and cannot decline. A period with no further change is described as stability within the observed window, not as proof that no later change will occur. For paired components, the effect of removing one component is compared when the other is present versus absent, using the same prespecified outcome scale and time horizon.
source_neutral.inferential_warrant: A reproducible loss of activation after a component is removed supports dependence on that component within the tested configuration, users and time window; it does not establish universal necessity. Successful unassisted activation without a component is a counterexample to the strict necessity of that component for that tested user and path. Slower activation with comparable later completion supports a contribution to timing, not demonstrated necessity for eventual completion. Removal effects that differ according to the setting of the other component support an interaction between the two. Joint removal producing a loss that is absent from either single removal is consistent with substitution or redundancy between the components. These response patterns distinguish candidate accounts of the flow, including a component being required before progress can continue, a component speeding progress, and one component making up for the absence of another. Effects that depend on context, or cumulative time courses of different conditions that cross one another, prevent a single feature ranking from expressing all tested contributions.
source_neutral.problem_decomposition: Units: (1) individual onboarding components, or bundles of components that cannot be separated from their dependencies; (2) configurations, consisting of the full redesign, each single-removal variant and joint-removal variants for selected pairs; (3) users, characterized by user group, entry checkpoint, prior experience and starting progress, randomly assigned to configurations, with fresh users for each variant; (4) outcome measures, consisting of activation defined observably, with executable activation kept distinct from prototype task completion, plus timestamped progress, errors, retries and assistance; (5) the prespecified observation window and burden limit. Relationships: the availability setting of a component is related to the time course of progress and to activation; dependencies among components determine which components can be tested separately and which are tested as a bundle; for pairs, the effect of removing one component is related to whether the other is present or absent; timing effects are separated from effects on eventual completion; candidate accounts (required for progression, speeding progress, one component compensating for another) are distinguished by the pattern of responses across configurations. The question of necessity is addressed per component or bundle within the tested configuration, and the question of what prevents a simple ranking is addressed through the pairwise present/absent comparisons and through differences in time courses.
source_neutral.next_inquiry: Identify the actual proposed components and their dependencies, since none are specified in the packet. Follow suspected interactions with the paired tests described, covering full, each single-removal and joint-removal configurations; do not extend those findings to combinations that were not tested. If manipulation fidelity or comparability of starting states fails, correct the setup and repeat the test. If progress measures are still changing at the time limit, or if uncertainty does not allow the candidate accounts to be distinguished, report the result as unresolved and run a longer, newly specified observation window or additional comparable cohorts.
source_neutral.limits: Noise, unequal starting knowledge, assistance, traffic differences, instrumentation errors and implementation defects can distort the recorded time courses. Completion rates near the minimum or maximum possible can conceal effects. Nonlinear behavior and interacting components can make a full removal of a component unrepresentative of smaller changes. Results depend on the tested user group, checkpoint, configuration, outcome scale and observation window. Success in a prototype supports claims about the simulated task unless real activation is available and measured. Absence of observed completion does not prove that completion is impossible, and single removals do not establish a globally minimal sufficient redesign. Conclusions about an inseparable component are bounded to the bundle it belongs to. The procedure assumes availability can be changed reproducibly with other intended conditions preserved. Stopping and halting conditions: individual observation ends at the prespecified time limit or participant burden limit, with early exits and assistance recorded explicitly and unobserved later outcomes not counted as established failures; if manipulation fidelity or starting-state comparability fails, attribution of differences to the named component stops until the setup is corrected and the test repeated; if measures are still changing at the time limit or uncertainty cannot distinguish the candidate accounts, the result is reported as unresolved. Findings from paired tests are not extended to untested combinations.
